messages:
olivia_support: customer reports 3x latency and unexpected egress to EU for a US-only tenant. requests show as routed to eu-central-1 even though they set region=us-west in their client. billing spike flagged. :warning:

olivia_support: customer says they are on mobile sdk v2.1.4 + an instrumentation layer. here's the raw header they captured: `X-Client-Region: dXMtd2VzdA==`

ingrid_engineer: wait, that's base64 for 'us-west' (:thinking: ). if our router expects plain tokens it'll treat that as unknown. any chance a sidecar or analytics layer is encoding headers?

olivia_support: they confirmed an analytics shim is base64-encoding metadata to avoid non-ASCII issues. they thought headers would be opaque.

devon_platform: can we get edge logs for a sample request id? need to see what the router saw and why it fell back.

olivia_support: pasted below (sanitized):
```
edge-router-bot: [edge-log] req_id=abc123 host=api.redwood.example path=/v1/generate X-Client-Region="dXMtd2VzdA==" lookup=FAILED fallback=eu-central-1 selected_node=eu-3 latency=912ms
edge-router-bot: [route-debug] decode_candidates=["dXMtd2VzdA=="] match_found=false
```
edge-router-bot: router attempted literal match on header token, no entry for 'dXMtd2VzdA==' -> applied configured fallback policy (nearest region = eu-central-1).

marc_sre: confirmed locally. repro with curl:
```
# reproducer
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Client-Region: dXMtd2VzdA==" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/models
# response headers show X-Selected-Edge: eu-central-1
```
ingrid_engineer: short-term mitigation options:
- ask customer to disable the analytics shim or stop base64-encoding the region header
- add server-side tolerant parsing: attempt a base64 decode for tokens matching base64 charset/padding and treat decoded value as candidate region (quick patch)

devon_platform: created internal issue INF-5821 and added a minimal patch plan: "router: try base64 decode of region header if literal lookup fails and decoded token matches known region list". linking PR once ready. assigning to @ingrid_engineer.

ingrid_engineer: I'll implement a safe decode with bounds checks (only if token length <= 32 and matches /^[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+$/). won't auto-fall back to decoding if token contains commas or other separators. aiming for review within 24h.

marc_sre: ops action: run a daily query for the next 7 days to find header tokens that look like base64 and count misroutes. also flag tenants with >10% cross-region routing for billing review.

olivia_support: customer ask: they want repro steps to validate and a temporary workaround. sending this now. include example Node snippet for them to test: 
```
// node repro: ensure header is NOT base64-encoded
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/models', {
  method: 'GET',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${TOKEN}`,
    'X-Client-Region': 'us-west' // not base64
  }
}).then(r => r.headers.forEach((v,k) => console.log(k,v)));
```
olivia_support: proposed customer message: "Disable the analytics header encoding or set the region via SDK config (example: Redwood.config({ region: 'us-west' })) to avoid router fallback."

devon_platform: will coordinate the patch rollout to canary edges first. once PR merged, we'll watch for reduced misroutes.

ingrid_engineer: PR opened: https://internal/redwood/INF-5821/PR45 (includes tests + feature flag).

olivia_support: OOO customer-facing notes: offered 48h credit window for impacted requests and requested permission to patch router heuristics. customer granted. :white_check_mark:

marc_sre: adding ticket to billing queue to review credits.

olivia_support: status: root cause = client-side base64 encoding of region header; short-term workaround = stop encoding or set SDK config; medium-term = router tolerant parse (PR45) rolling out. ETA: patch review + canary deploy 24-48h. I'll update thread with canary results. :eyes:
